problem: Procedural simulators, language-guided scene generators and 4D generators live in separate representations and authoring pipelines. Getting from user conditions (text, mask, photo) to one editable scene whose geometry, actor motion, camera motion and physics state agree is still manual work and rarely reusable at scale.
motivation: Embodied agents need environments that are visually diverse, physically interactive and time-varying. Existing procedural simulators lack controllable dynamics, and 4D generators output view-rendering representations without explicit geometry or collision. A unified explicit, editable representation would allow reproducible failures and independently tunable difficulty axes.
key_idea: Route four scene-realization paths (native indoor, native outdoor, text/mask layout, single-image real-to-sim) into one shared geometry-grounded Stage and provenance-tracking WorldState, on which animated actors, collision-free trajectories, cameras, OpenUSD physics export and navigation tasks are all derived.
insight: Keeping the representation explicit and procedural (object identity, support, walkability, material-derived physics) lets one pipeline serve animation, camera planning, simulation and automatic task generation without per-scene mesh work. The benchmark shows partial progress runs well ahead of success (e.g. Qwen L3 SP 15.0 vs SR 4.5; Gemini L3 27.7 vs 18.2), pointing to failures after phase transitions. The tiers also separate the models, especially on blind starts (L1 SR 57.5 vs 16.8). Comparisons are diagnostic, not controlled ablations, and no ablation of the pipeline itself is reported.
method: Constrained LLM parsing: writes scene, actor, action, goal and camera intent into a schema-validated 4D specification.

Four scene routes: native indoor/outdoor Infinigen generation (8 biomes, seed recorded), text/mask layouts normalized to a Canonical Layout IR then built by procedural factories, and single-image real-to-sim (depth, segmentation, 3D proxies, agent-grounded procedural assets, material alignment).

Shared Stage extraction: metric support grid with walkability set W, object inventory and collision geometry; per-actor free space is Erode(W, r_i); outdoor uses a coarse-to-final loop with replanning.
4D actors: LLM maps actions to mocap clips; imported characters are measured (stature, radius, speed); A* trajectory planning with reactive multi-agent separation, then baking with foot grounding.
Geometry-valid camera synthesis: 9 composable motion primitives, geometry-exact vs fast (11 transforms) planning modes, occlusion as a soft cost, and framing thresholds of 80%/90%.
Physics-ready OpenUSD export to Isaac Sim: material-derived density/friction, static colliders, rigid bodies, and humans as kinematic capsules, verified headlessly.
4DSynth-Nav generation: scene probing, task generation under five invariants, and spawn validation with PhysX sweeps and frustum checks.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking (frozen, vLLM) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (frozen) as benchmark agents; pipeline uses LLM/VLM agents, Depth Anything 3, SAM 3, SAM 3D
setting.training_data: none (training-free; pipeline and benchmark evaluation only)
setting.observation: egocentric RGB, up to 3 recent frames at 960x540, path-traced, plus text instruction and action feedback
setting.action_space: low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT/RIGHT 15°, TILT_UP/DOWN 5°, PAUSE, PICK_UP, PUT_DOWN, DONE; up to 5 actions per plan
setting.privileged: none for agents (privileged scene info used only for task generation and validation)

numbers.extra: 150 actions or 50 VLM calls per episode; 333 tasks

numbers_note: Only the paper's own new benchmark (4DSynth-Nav) is evaluated; no standard benchmarks. Per-tier rows (L1, L2, L3) exist for both models; only some are listed here.
results: On 4DSynth-Nav, Gemini 3.1 Pro reaches 33.3% SR / 40.7% SP versus 13.2% / 22.4% for Qwen3-VL-30B, with goal distance dropping from 4.27 m to 2.68 m. Both fail most tasks, with the largest gap on blind-start L1 (57.5 vs 16.8 SR) and the hardest tier L3 (18.2 vs 4.5 SR). SP well above SR indicates stalling after early subtasks.
limitations: Real-to-sim and scene-synthesis results are qualitative only (VIGA comparison), with no metric fidelity or controllability evaluation; the authors plan to quantify these later.
Benchmark uses only two VLMs, and the two differ in many ways, so the comparison is diagnostic. Dynamic humans are non-reactive kinematic capsules and objects are not articulated.
Benchmark covers only indoor Infinigen scenes and only navigation and pick-and-place, with no learned-agent or robot baselines.
